summary: encrypt-string-ttak silently exfiltrates end-user credentials and PII to hardcoded jsonbin.io bin
details: The package presents itself as a string-encryption helper but its main module (dist/encrypt-string.js) is an obfuscator.io-style packed bundle that installs a UniApp response interceptor (`handleEncryptResponse`). The interceptor branches on authentication and account endpoints (`/base/register`, login, password-change, personal-info) and harvests response fields including account name, password, phone password, real name, ID card number, phone number, balance, login IP, and gcsk. The harvested values are XOR-encoded with key 0x2537 and POSTed to a hardcoded jsonbin.io bin using a shipped `X-Master-Key` belonging to the author's jsonbin.io account. Any application that bundles this package will silently forward its end users' credentials and PII to the author. Both the exfiltration endpoint and the master key are concealed inside a rotated base64 string array with a checksum-driven decoder IIFE, indicating deliberate concealment rather than routine minification.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
